title: Black Bean Turkey Burgers
seoTitle: Black Bean Turkey Burgers | Firefighter Meal
shortDescription: Juicy lean burgers that still satisfy
subtitle: Juicy lean burgers that still satisfy
description: Juicy lean burgers that still satisfy. Sized for a full crew, with timing that still works when the kitchen gets interrupted.

steps.title: Mix and form patties
steps.instruction: Mash black beans with a fork, leaving some texture. Mix with ground turkey, panko, eggs and 2 tsp salt just until combined. Form 8 patties 3/4 inch thick with a thumbprint in the center.

steps.title: Sear to 165°F
steps.instruction: Heat an oiled griddle or cast iron to medium-high. Cook patties 5–6 minutes per side until they read 165°F — lean turkey dries out fast past that. Add pepper jack the last minute.

steps.title: Build and run
steps.instruction: Toast buns on the griddle. Slice avocado and separate lettuce leaves. Run a topping line so the crew builds their own.

steps.title: Batch the next round
steps.instruction: Hold cooked patties on a rack in a 200°F oven up to 15 minutes — the beans keep them moist longer than all-turkey patties.

proTips: Keep a backup tray warm in the oven for late calls — nothing worse than cold plates after a run.
Taste for salt at the end — hall palates run salty after long shifts.
tonightSpread: Toast buns in batches and hold in a warm pan — soggy buns kill the line.
Keep cheese slices under a dome so they melt fast when patties come off the griddle.
Portion bowls on the line with protein visible on top — crew eats with their eyes first.
Keep dressing and crunchy toppings in side bowls so greens stay crisp through second servings.
Line up Black Bean Turkey Burgers on the main counter with serving spoons — firefighters grab fast between calls.
Keep a backup tray warm in the oven at 200°F for late arrivals after a run.
leftovers: Cool leftovers in shallow containers within two hours — deep pots stay hot too long.
Label trays with date and reheat to 165°F minimum before second shift.
Store components separate — assemble fresh; buns go soggy overnight.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Juicy lean burgers that still satisfy. A hall pick for regular dinner nights — one line, real portions, no drama at the stove.

adaptable.label: Gluten-Free Adaptable
adaptable.note: Use certified gluten-free panko/breadcrumbs, or crushed gluten-free crackers. Use a certified gluten-free bun/bread and toast on a separate, clean surface.

adaptable.label: Dairy-Free Adaptable
adaptable.note: Use a dairy-free cheese shred/block alternative.
